hook: In the 1960s, fishing boats worked the Aral Sea, one of the largest lakes on Earth. Today rusting hulls sit on a dry, salty plain. The water went to cotton fields in the desert. Farming can feed a region and, at the same time, remake its land and water.

options: Supplying water to crops by canals, pipes or sprinklers
Cutting a slope into flat steps
Letting a field rest for many years
prereq.why: Irrigation brings water where rain alone is not enough.

options: Using resources so that future generations can still meet their needs
Using as many resources as possible now
Moving people from farms to cities
prereq.why: Sustainability balances use today against needs in the future.

figure.caption: Years of irrigation in a hot, dry place can leave salt in the soil.

chain.cause: Planners diverted the rivers feeding the Aral Sea to irrigate cotton
Irrigation water evaporated from desert fields
chain.effect: salt built up in the soil

chain.cause: The dry seabed was exposed to wind
chain.effect: salty dust blew onto farmland and towns

ideas: Practices that change landscapes: slash and burn, deforestation, terracing, irrigation, draining wetlands, pastoral nomadism.
Environmental effects: pollution and dead zones from fertilizer runoff, salinization from irrigating dry land, desertification of dry lands, loss of habitat.
Conservation: terraces, contour plowing, no-till farming, cover crops, drip irrigation.
Societal effects: changing diets (more meat, more feed crops), economic purpose (subsistence or commercial) and who does farm work.

misconception.wrong: Changing a landscape for farming always harms the environment.
misconception.right: Effects can be positive or negative. Terracing changes a slope and also conserves soil; irrigation feeds millions but can cause salinization.

summary: Farming changes landscapes through slash and burn, deforestation, terracing, irrigation and wetland draining. Its environmental effects include pollution, salinization, desertification and habitat loss, offset in part by conservation practices. Its societal effects include changing diets, the purpose of farming and who does the work.
